messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED — Elevated 503/timeout rates seen for zenbridge private VPC egress (dedicated pool rz-3). Paging on-call.

devon: on it. paging logs + quick impact check. @zenbridge-sre can you confirm anything changed on your side? any recent SG/NAT changes?

zenbridge-sre: no changes from our side. Noticed ~11:10 UTC some requests failing to downstream payment gateways; we opened a support ticket.

maria: I see 5xx spike from our NLB outbound targets. Metrics: target group tz-zenbridge-out shows unhealthy hosts jumping from 2 -> 12, connection resets. Rolling 503s on the ingress path. Links: https://telemetry/redwood/rg/zenbridge/requests

irina: looking at control plane — dedicated pool rz-3 CPU/GPU okay. Network telemetry shows a burst of SYN_RETRY + TCP resets to 3rd-party IPs originating from tenant subnets. Could be conntrack/NAT exhaustion on the tenant NATGW instance.

pradeep: adding hypothesis: customer uses private NLB with proxy protocol into our private agent. If conntrack table is full on NAT instance we will see midstream resets. Can someone check conntrack + nat metrics on the customer's VPC gateway?

sam: run this on the gateway host (if you have access):

```
sudo conntrack -S
sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
sudo watch -n1 'conntrack -L | wc -l'
```

zenbridge-sre: we don't have direct host shell for managed NATGW, but our cloud console shows NATGW ephemeral ports used at ~98%. Trying to scale/replace.

devon: ok. Immediate mitigation plan options:
- divert zenbridge egress through fallback NLB in us-west-2 (fallthrough) via Route53 change
- temporarily increase NATGW capacity / replace NATGW
- route high-risk external hosts through a separate egress pool with dedicated NAT

Which is fastest to reduce customer impact? Route53 switch could be fastest if DNS TTLs allow.

maria: TTLs for the internal alias are 30s for this customer, we can do weighted failover to fallback NLB with 90/10 then 100/0. I can push the Route53 change once we confirm fallback healthy.

pradeep: before doing DNS flip, ensure fallback NLB target group's healthchecks match — last time we had mismatch and caused opaque 502s. Check health check path and headers.

sam: health check for tz-zenbridge-out-fallback is /healthz and expects 200; current shows 200. Verified with curl from our internal probe:

```
curl -sS -D - http://tz-zenbridge-out-fallback.internal:8080/healthz | head
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

irina: also noticed a security group misrule was recently rolled in a canary that blocked ephemeral ports 49152-65535 from our agents back to the NATGW — that would surface as failed connections. I see the rule in sg-zenbridge-proxy: outbound allow 443 only, missing ephemeral range.

devon: if SG is the root cause, changing SG is simplest. zenbridge-sre, can you relax the outbound SG to include 1024-65535 to the NATGW CIDR for the short term?

zenbridge-sre: we can open a temporary rule to allow ephemeral port range to the NATGW. Applying now — will take ~12s to propagate.

maria: propagation seen. Metrics dropping: 5xx rate reduced from 18% -> 4% in the last 60s. Nice.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident update — customer impact reduced. Severity: P2 -> monitoring. Next action: follow-up RCA and permanent SG fix.

pradeep: I'll coordinate a follow-up change to make SG rules explicit for ephemeral ports and add a test harness to validate before canary. Also propose adding conntrack headroom alarms on managed NAT resources.

sam: log snippet from proxy agent around spike (sanitized):

```
2026-03-15T11:09:12Z proxy[pid=2321] WARN client_conn reset_by_peer ip=10.2.14.23:34512 -> 52.88.12.101:443
2026-03-15T11:09:13Z proxy[pid=2321] WARN client_conn resource_exhausted conntrack=98304/98304
```

irina: timeline + customer impact notes for handoff:
- 11:08 UTC: increase in TCP resets & 5xx for zenbridge dedicated pool
- 11:10 UTC: zenbridge reports external payment gateway failures
- 11:12 UTC: identified high ephemeral port usage / conntrack saturation on NATGW
- 11:14 UTC: SG rule missing ephemeral range discovered (canary change)
- 11:16 UTC: temporary SG relaxation applied by customer — immediate improvement
- 11:20 UTC: Route53 failover not executed (no longer needed)

devon: handing off to on-call for the next 4 hours. Current state: reduced customer impact, monitoring for regression, follow-up tasks created. Who's taking primary on-call until 15:30 UTC? @maria or @pradeep?

maria: I can take the on-call handoff. I'll own the follow-up and coordinate the post-incident change with zenbridge.

zenbridge-sre: thanks team. We'll schedule a maintenance window to make the SG change permanent and request assistance if we need config templates.

devon: action items (short):
- maria: own customer comms + permanent SG change (ticket created RZ-INC-4578)
- pradeep: add conntrack headroom alert and runbook
- sam: validate fallback target group healthchecks + add preflight checks to rollout pipeline
- irina: capture network traces and attach to RCA

incident-bot: :page_with_curl: Postmortem draft started: https://playbook/incidents/RZ-INC-4578. Severity P2. Assigning to maria.

maria: acknowledged. I'll post a summary to #customer-success and follow up with zenbridge SRE with proposed change window.

devon: closing active paging. If errors spike again, escalate immediately and we can push DNS failover.

zenbridge-sre: appreciate the quick ops help. We'll monitor and keep you posted.

maria: low-friction summary for handoff log: "Conntrack/NAT ephemeral exhaustion due to missing SG ephemeral range after a canary rule. Temporary SG relaxation mitigated. Root fix: permanent SG rule + conntrack headroom alarms + preflight tests for SG canaries."]
